title: Many mansions (John 14:1–6)
hookLine: let not your heart be troubled; I am the way, the truth and the life

cards: Arriving somewhere strange is easier when someone says, we've set up the spare room for you. Clean sheets, a towel folded on the bed. The bag isn't even unpacked, and already there's a place for you.
At the supper, Jesus has just told Peter that he'll deny him three times before the rooster crows. It's a hard thing to hear. And the very next thing Jesus says is about rooms.

teach.h: LET NOT YOUR HEART BE TROUBLED.
teach.b: In the Douay-Rheims: "Let not your heart be troubled. You believe in God, believe also in me. In my Father's house there are many mansions. If not, I would have told you: because I go to prepare a place for you."
Mansions sounds like marble and gated driveways. In the Douay's older English, the word just meant a dwelling, a place to stay; the Latin behind it is mansiones, lodgings. So this isn't real estate.
It's: there is room for you to stay, and I'm going ahead to get it ready.
Then Thomas says out loud what he doesn't understand: Lord, we don't know where you're going, so how can we know the way?
And Jesus answers: "I am the way, and the truth, and the life. No man cometh to the Father, but by me." Thomas asked for directions. He gets a person.
And notice who heard it: frightened men, one of whom was about to deny him and all of whom, he will soon tell them, would be scattered.
He doesn't wait for them to be brave first. The room is ready before they are.

how: John 14:1–6 is one of the Gospel readings offered for Catholic funeral Masses, and the Church prays daily for the dying and the dead, especially in November.

games.q: you're Thomas. Jesus says you know the way to where he's going. you don't. what do you do?
o: say so: Lord, we don't know where you're going.
games.why: Thomas admits it out loud, and gets the answer: I am the way, and the truth, and the life.

practice: Think of someone who is afraid of dying, someone sick right now, someone very old, someone grieving, or a fear you carry yourself, and picture them in a quiet room, a light on, a chair ready.
Don't try to argue the fear away; just keep them company in your mind. If you pray, pray for them with Jesus's words, let not your heart be troubled; if not, simply hold them kindly.

wordCard.voice: Many mansions. In his Father's house there are many places to stay, and Jesus goes ahead to prepare one. Today's word.
